blocks.html: Greetings and Salutations!

items.html: Paul, and Silvanus, and Timothy, unto the church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We give thanks to God always for you all, making mention of you in our prayers;
Remembering without ceasing your work of faith, and labour of love, and patience of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, in the sight of God and our Father;

blocks.html:
From Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy

to the church in Thessalonica.

items.html: Knowing, brethren beloved, your election of God.
For our gospel came not unto you in word only, but also in power, and in the Holy Ghost, and in much assurance; as ye know what manner of men we were among you for your sake.
And ye became followers of us, and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Ghost.
So that ye were ensamples to all that believe in Macedonia and Achaia.
For from you sounded out the word of the Lord not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every place your faith to God-ward is spread abroad; so that we need not to speak any thing.
For they themselves shew of us what manner of entering in we had unto you, and how ye turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God;

blocks.html: We know you've been elected by God. [1]

items.html: And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.

blocks.html:
Now you're waiting for Jesus to return from heaven. [2]

God raised him from the dead, [3]

and he saved us from the wrath to come. [4]

footnotes.html:
Knowing ... your election of God (v.4)

The elect and the damned are predestined by God.

To wait for his Son from heaven (v.10a)

Paul expected Jesus to return during the life of his contemporaries.

His Son ... whom he raised from the dead. (v.10b)

Who raised Jesus from the dead?

The wrath to come (v.10c)

God is planning a messy mass murder in "the wrath to come" and only Jesus can save you from it.

blocks.html: We were holy, just, and perfect among you

items.html: For yourselves, brethren, know our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain:
But even after that we had suffered before, and were shamefully entreated, as ye know, at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak unto you the gospel of God with much contention.

blocks.html:
We were shamefully treated at Philippi,

but we spoke boldly nonetheless.

items.html: For our exhortation was not of deceit, nor of uncleanness, nor in guile:
But as we were allowed of God to be put in trust with the gospel, even so we speak; not as pleasing men, but God, which trieth our hearts.

blocks.html: We didn't try to deceive anyone with uncleanness.

items.html: For neither at any time used we flattering words, as ye know, nor a cloke of covetousness; God is witness:

blocks.html:
We didn't use flattering words.

God is our witness.

items.html: Nor of men sought we glory, neither of you, nor yet of others, when we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ.

blocks.html: We didn't seek glory or make a burden of ourselves.

items.html: But we were gentle among you, even as a nurse cherisheth her children:
So being affectionately desirous of you, we were willing to have imparted unto you, not the gospel of God only, but also our own souls, because ye were dear unto us.

blocks.html: But we were gentle among you.

items.html: For ye remember, brethren, our labour and travail: for labouring night and day, because we would not be chargeable unto any of you, we preached unto you the gospel of God.

blocks.html:
You remember how hard we worked for you,

laboring night and day.

items.html: Ye are witnesses, and God also, how holily and justly and unblameably we behaved ourselves among you that believe:
As ye know how we exhorted and comforted and charged every one of you, as a father doth his children,
That ye would walk worthy of God, who hath called you unto his kingdom and glory.

For this cause also thank we God without ceasing, because, when ye received the word of God which ye heard of us, ye received it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth, the word of God, which effectually worketh also in you that believe.

blocks.html: You and God saw how holy, just, and perfect we were. [1]
The Jews killed Jesus

items.html: For ye, brethren, became followers of the churches of God which in Judea are in Christ Jesus: for ye also have suffered like things of your own countrymen, even as they have of the Jews:

blocks.html: The Jews killed Jesus and their own prophets [2]

items.html: Who both killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God, and are contrary to all men:

blocks.html:
and they persecuted us.

They don't please God and are contrary to everyone.

items.html: Forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles that they might be saved, to fill up their sins alway: for the wrath is come upon them to the uttermost.

blocks.html: God's wrath will be especially hard on them.
We would have visited you, but Satan stopped us

items.html: But we, brethren, being taken from you for a short time in presence, not in heart, endeavoured the more abundantly to see your face with great desire.
Wherefore we would have come unto you, even I Paul, once and again; but Satan hindered us.

blocks.html:
We would have come to you, even I Paul,

but Satan stopped us.

items.html: For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even ye in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?
For ye are our glory and joy.

blocks.html: When Jesus comes, you'll be there to greet him. [3]

footnotes.html:
Ye are witnesses, and God also, how holily and justly and unblameably we behaved ourselves among you. (v.10)

Paul, with his usual modesty, proclaims that he is holy, just, and blameless.

The Jews ... killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God, and are contrary to all men. (vv.14-15)

Paul accuses the Jews of killing Jesus, along with their own prophets, displeasing God, and being "contrary to all men." He concludes that the wrath of God will "come upon them to the uttermost."

Are not even ye in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? (v.19)

Paul believed that those alive in 49 CE would live to see Jesus return to earth.

blocks.html:
You've already endured the tribulation

(so Jesus will be coming soon)

items.html: Wherefore when we could no longer forbear, we thought it good to be left at Athens alone;
And sent Timothy, our brother, and minister of God, and our fellow labourer in the gospel of Christ, to establish you, and to comfort you concerning your faith:
That no man should be moved by these afflictions: for yourselves know that we are appointed thereunto.
For verily, when we were with you, we told you before that we should suffer tribulation; even as it came to pass, and ye know.
For this cause, when I could no longer forbear, I sent to know your faith, lest by some means the tempter have tempted you, and our labour be in vain.
But now when Timothy came from you unto us, and brought us good tidings of your faith and charity, and that ye have good remembrance of us always, desiring greatly to see us, as we also to see you:
Therefore, brethren, we were comforted over you in all our affliction and distress by your faith:
For now we live, if ye stand fast in the Lord.
For what thanks can we render to God again for you, for all the joy wherewith we joy for your sakes before our God;
Night and day praying exceedingly that we might see your face, and might perfect that which is lacking in your faith?
Now God himself and our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way unto you.
And the Lord make you to increase and abound in love one toward another, and toward all men, even as we do toward you:

blocks.html:
We told you before that you'd have to endure tribulation,

and you have. [1]

items.html: To the end he may stablish your hearts unblameable in holiness before God, even our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.

blocks.html:
When Jesus comes,

he'll establish your hearts in holiness before God.

footnotes.html:
We told you before that we should suffer tribulation; even as it came to pass. (v.4)

He may stablish your hearts ... at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. (v.13)

Paul thought that the tribulation that he believed would precede Jesus's coming had already passed, and that Jesus would come during his lifetime.

blocks.html:
Know how to possess your vessel

(in holiness and honor)

items.html: Furthermore then we beseech you, brethren, and exhort you by the Lord Jesus, that as ye have received of us how ye ought to walk and to please God, so ye would abound more and more.
For ye know what commandments we gave you by the Lord Jesus.

blocks.html: You know the commandments that we gave you from Jesus.

items.html: For this is the will of God, even your sanctification, that ye should abstain from fornication:

blocks.html: This is the will of God: Don't fornicate. [1]

items.html: That every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour;

blocks.html: Every man should know how to possess his vessel in holiness and honor. [2]

items.html: Not in the lust of concupiscence, even as the Gentiles which know not God:

blocks.html: Don't be filled with lust like the Gentiles.

items.html: That no man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter: because that the Lord is the avenger of all such, as we also have forewarned you and testified.
For God hath not called us unto uncleanness, but unto holiness.
He therefore that despiseth, despiseth not man, but God, who hath also given unto us his holy Spirit.
But as touching brotherly love ye need not that I write unto you: for ye yourselves are taught of God to love one another.
And indeed ye do it toward all the brethren which are in all Macedonia: but we beseech you, brethren, that ye increase more and more;
And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you;
That ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that ye may have lack of nothing.

blocks.html: And don't take something that belongs to someone else. [3]
The rapture (?)

items.html: But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.

blocks.html:
Don't worry about believers who have died.

They're not like dead non-believers who have no hope. [4]

items.html: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Jesus will God bring with him.

blocks.html: When Jesus returns, he'll bring dead believers with him.

items.html: For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep.

blocks.html:
Jesus told me that when he returns,

those of us who are alive won't precede the dead. [5]

items.html: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:

blocks.html:
Jesus will descend with a shout,

with the voice of an archangel. [6]

A trumpet will sound, [7] and dead believers will rise first.

items.html: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.

blocks.html:
Then those of us who are alive will be raised up into the clouds

to meet Jesus in the air and be with him forever. [8]

items.html: Wherefore comfort one another with these words.

blocks.html: Comfort one another with these words.

footnotes.html:
Ye should abstain from fornication. (v.3)

Is it wrong to have sex outside of marriage?

Every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour (v.4)

Every man should know how to possess his penis or his wife (depending on the translation) in a holy way.

No man go beyond and defraud his brother in any matter (v.6)

This seems to be saying that no male believer should have sex with another male believer's wife.

Is it wrong to steal?

Others ... have no hope. (v.13)

Christians shouldn't mourn the death of their fellow believers. They'll be OK; you'll see them later in heaven. The people you should mourn are dead nonbelievers. They have no hope (because they're going to hell).

We which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep. (v.15)

First Thessalonians was one of the first Christian writings, yet already (ca.50 CE) believers were getting impatient about Jesus' supposed return. Their fellow believers were dying and yet Jesus still hadn't come. What the hell is taking him? And what happens to dead believers? Will they get to see Jesus return?

For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel. (v.16a)

Jehovah's Witnesses: From this verse and Jude 9, the Jehovah's Witnesses figure that Jesus is really the archangel Michael.

The trump of God (v.16b)

But the JWs are wrong about that. Donald Trump is the trump of God -- or so says WND, anyway. Donald Trump is God's final warning to America.

We which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air (v.17)

Christians get the idea of the rapture from this verse. (Paul thought he'd live to see it.)

blocks.html: When Jesus comes, it'll be like childbirth

items.html: But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you.

blocks.html: But I don't have to tell you about the times and seasons.

items.html: For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.

blocks.html: You know the Lord's day will come as a thief in the night.

items.html: For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.

blocks.html:
When people are saying, "Everything's fine",

the world will be destroyed like a woman in childbirth.

And they won't escape.

items.html: But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief.

blocks.html:
But you'll be okay.

That day won't surprise you like a thief.

items.html: Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness.

blocks.html: You're the children of light.

items.html: Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.

blocks.html:
So don't go to sleep.

Watch and be sober.

items.html: For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night.

blocks.html: People sleep and get drunk at night.

items.html: But let us, who are of the day, be sober, putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation.

blocks.html:
But we day-people will be sober,

wearing the breastplate of faith and love,

with salvation as a helmet.

items.html: For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ,

blocks.html:
God won't hurt us with his wrath.

He's saved us through Jesus.

items.html: Who died for us, that, whether we wake or sleep, we should live together with him.
Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do.
And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you;
And to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. And be at peace among yourselves.

blocks.html:
He died for us,

and dead or alive, we'll live with him.
Prove all things, hold fast to that which is good

items.html: Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.

blocks.html: Help the weak and be patient with everyone.

items.html: See that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all men.

blocks.html:
Don't be evil to those who are evil to you.

Do good to everyone.

items.html: Rejoice evermore.

blocks.html: Be happy.

items.html: Pray without ceasing.

blocks.html: Pray all the time.

items.html: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

blocks.html: Be thankful.

items.html: Quench not the Spirit.

blocks.html: Don't quench the spirit.

items.html: Despise not prophesyings.

blocks.html: Don't despise prophesyings.

items.html: Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.

blocks.html:
Test every belief to see if it's true or false. [1]

Hold on to what is good.

items.html: Abstain from all appearance of evil.

blocks.html: Stay away from anything that even appears to be evil.

items.html: And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it.

blocks.html: I pray you'll be blameless on the day Jesus returns. [2]

items.html: Brethren, pray for us.

blocks.html: Pray for us.

items.html: Greet all the brethren with an holy kiss.

blocks.html: Give everyone a holy kiss.

items.html: I charge you by the Lord that this epistle be read unto all the holy brethren.

blocks.html: Read this letter to all the holy people.

items.html: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

blocks.html: Amen.

Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. (v.21)

Should we believe everything?

Should we think for ourselves?

Paul prays that the Thessalonians will be good until Jesus returns, which implies that he expected this to happen within their lifetimes.
